train.demo_note: Quick demo preset: width 0.5 · train subset 0.2 · 3 epochs (a set of input values, not a separate model)
train.empty: No training is running. Configure it on the left and start training.
train.hint.arch: The image classifier from the official Keras example, scaled down for 32×32 images. It cannot be changed in this PoC.
train.hint.augment: Shows each training image slightly changed every time, so the model still recognizes things that look a bit different. flip: mirror left–right, rotation: rotate up to ±36°, translation: shift up to 10% in any direction.
train.hint.batch: How many images the model looks at before each update. Larger is faster per epoch but uses more memory. 128 is recommended on an 8GB Mac.
train.hint.dataset: fine: recognize 100 kinds of objects (e.g. apple, pear). coarse: recognize 20 broader groups of them (e.g. fruit_and_vegetables). The images are the same; only the level of the answer differs.
train.hint.device: auto uses the Mac's GPU (Metal) and falls back to the CPU if there is none. On an M2, the GPU is about 1.9× faster than the CPU.
train.hint.dropout: During training, randomly switches off part of the signal right before classification (0.25 = 25%). This reduces overfitting, i.e. the model memorizing the training images. 0 = off.
train.hint.epochs: How many times the model goes through all training images. Accuracy rises with more epochs, then stops improving. Time grows in proportion (full data on GPU: about 1.5 min per epoch at width 0.5, 3.2 min at 1.0).
train.hint.lr: How big each update step is. Too large makes training unstable; too small makes learning slow. If unsure, keep the default 0.0003.
train.hint.name: A label to find this model in the list. Leave it blank to name it from the settings automatically, e.g. 'xception_mini w1.0 (fine)'.
train.hint.patience: Stops training early, saving time, if val acc does not improve for this many epochs in a row. Either way, the model from the best epoch is saved. 0 = always run all epochs.
train.hint.seed: Starting number for the random steps (data split, shuffling, augmentation, initial weights). The same seed gives the same conditions, so you can repeat an experiment. Keep it fixed when comparing settings.
train.hint.subset: Share of the training images actually used. 0.2 uses only 20%: about 5× faster, but less accurate. Meant for demos; class proportions stay the same.
train.hint.val: This share of the training images is held back: it is not used for learning, only to check the score (val acc) after each epoch. The best-scoring epoch's model is the one kept. The 10,000 test images are used separately on the Evaluate page.
train.hint.width: Model size. A larger model can learn finer details but is slower. About 0.33M / 0.69M / 1.19M parameters; 0.5 trains about 2× faster than 1.0.
train.sub_html: Trains a single architecture, xception_mini: the Keras example's make_model adapted to 32×32. Models differ only in width and training settings.
train.toast_demo: Filled in the quick demo preset.
train.toast_done: Training finished. You can evaluate and test the model from the model list.
